newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli official says violence against Arabs common.
newsitem.headline: Israeli official says violence against Arabs common.

text.p: Israel's attorney-general said on Wednesday incidents of police brutality against Palestinians like that captured on video last month were widespread.

"After reviewing the figures issued to me...I am convinced that we're talking about a severe and widespread phenomenon," said Michael Ben-Yair in a letter obtained by Reuters sent to the internal security minister a week after a video was broadcast showing two border policemen beating Palestinians.
"The experience that investigators accumulated indicates that this is a phenomenon and not just an aberration."
His remarks contrasted with the reaction by other Israeli officials to the incident, filmed by an amateur video cameraman.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had condemned the incident but said it was rare.
Palestinians frequently complain about abuse by border policemen who patrol the West Bank and Gaza Strip, which Israel captured and has occupied since the 1967 Middle East war.

Internal Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told Israel Radio in response to the letter: "We cannot accept this in our society...but we must also refrain from pouncing on these people and placing all the blame on them."

An Israeli court charged the two border policemen this week with aggravated assault and abuse of authority. Four other border policemen were charged this week with beating a Palestinian unconscious after detaining him last June.

In a separate development, Israeli ministers extended by three months authorisation for the Shin Bet security service to use force in interrogation of Palestinians when it appears a guerrilla attack is imminent, Israel Radio said.
The prime minister's office refused to comment on the report.
